point_one_role_text: Use the north–south comparison to make the discovery surprising: Saturn’s north-polar hexagon has persisted for more than 40 years, while earlier Hubble and Cassini observations found no comparable long-lived polygonal wave in the south. This frames the decagon as evidence that Saturn’s two polar jet systems can behave very differently, rather than as a simple southern counterpart to the hexagon.

point_two_role_text: Translate the striking shape into atmospheric physics by presenting the decagon as a meandering wave embedded in a curved jet, rather than as a literal polygonal object or an ordinary cloud formation. Use the competing explanations—a periodic disturbance near the jet top or forcing by the nearby dark anticyclonic vortex—to turn the image into a question about how Saturn’s polar circulation is organized.
